payload.acceptance_criteria:
When basicly worktree cleanup removes a lane whose record is closed and whose landing merge commit is on main, then it also deletes the lane's remote branch, and it refuses by name when that proof is missing
When basicly worktree merge --mode ci ends by success, refusal or failure, then no land/LANE/N branch it pushed stays on origin
When a lane is replaced by a lane that landed, then cleanup of the replaced lane deletes its local and remote branch on that proof
payload.description:
## Context
When a lane lands or is replaced, I want its remote branch and every land proof branch removed by the tool, so origin holds only live work. 2026-11-19: origin had 42 branches besides main; the owner ran a 25-line delete script by hand. Causes: basicly worktree cleanup deletes the local branch only; worktree merge deletes land/LANE/N only on success (land/dev-orch-names/1 and land/dev-pipe-advice/1 stayed after failed --mode ci landings, and the stale ref then refused the next landing's candidate push); a re-cut lane (-2, -3, -r2) leaves the old branch, which is not an ancestor of main. Orchestrator decision 2026-11-19 19:48 UTC (owner request in the basicly window: clean up after yourself). Built by the repair session after repair-hooks-cut.
payload.title: Clean up a landed lane's remote branch and every land proof branch

payload.acceptance_criteria: When a session finishes or basicly check runs, then every local or remote lane branch or worktree whose record is closed, or that is older than 24 hours, is listed with the cleanup command, and the finish refuses until each is removed or carries a stated reason
payload.description:
## Context
When a session finishes, I want stale lanes and branches named and refused, so cleanup cannot be forgotten. Owner rule 2026-11-19: clean up after yourself. Depends on the cleanup tool fix. Orchestrator decision 2026-11-19 19:48 UTC; built by the repair session.
payload.title: Refuse a session finish while landed or stale lanes and branches remain
